Q: Formula working in Excel, but not in Google Sheets A:

It looks as though the purpose of the formula is to find the first value in column A where columns E and F satisfy a couple of conditions.

In this situation, Aggregate was used in older versions of Excel because you didn't need to enter it as an array formula using CtrlShiftEnter

Now in both Google Sheets and Excel you can use an Index/match combo, Xlookup or perhaps a filter which would look like this in GS:

=ARRAY_CONSTRAIN(filter('Master Entries'!A3:A250,'Master Entries'!F3:F250="x",'Master Entries'!E3:E250=C2),1,1)

or

=INDEX(FILTER('Master Entries'!A3:A250,'Master Entries'!F3:F250="x",'Master Entries'!E3:E250=C2),1)

Note

The filter function works slightly differently in Excel as it only takes a single list of 'include' criteria. The following should work in Excel and GS:

=INDEX(FILTER('Master Entries'!A3:A250,('Master Entries'!F3:F250="x")*('Master Entries'!E3:E250=C2)),1)
